title: Who Improves the Robot? Toward Physical Recursive Self-Improvement
abstract: arXiv:2610.18842v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Robots are increasingly autonomous in task execution, yet their improvement remains largely human-driven. This study investigates Physical Recursive Self-Improvement (Physical RSI), in which physical experience guides lasting updates to both a robot's capabilities and its improvement procedure, making subsequent improvement more effective across tasks. Physical RSI faces challenges from noisy observations, continuous dynamics, costly trials, and irreversible consequences. We present an L0-L5 framework that differentiates capability-level from meta-level updates and within-task from across-task gains, reserving L5 for independently verified recursive gain. We study existing methods around harness adaptation and model training, alongside safety and control mechanisms that govern execution and successive updates. Our analysis reveals that, despite substantial progress in self-improvement, the surveyed literature does not yet demonstrate Phy

translated_title: 谁在改进机器人？迈向物理递归自我改进
translated_abstract: 机器人在任务执行中日益自主，但其改进在很大程度上仍由人类驱动。本研究探讨了物理递归自我改进，即通过物理经验对机器人的能力及其改进过程本身进行持久性更新，从而使后续改进在各类任务中更加有效。物理RSI面临着噪声观测、连续动力学、高成本试验以及不可逆后果等挑战。我们提出了一个L0-L5分级框架，以区分能力层面的更新与元层面的更新、任务内收益与跨任务收益，并将L5保留给经过独立验证的递归增益。我们围绕工具适配与模型训练两条路线研究了现有方法，同时考察了规范执行与连续更新的安全与控制机制。我们的分析表明，尽管自我改进领域已取得重大进展，但所调研的文献尚未真正实现物理RSI。
tldr: 该研究提出物理递归自我改进（Physical RSI）的概念及L0-L5分级框架，区分机器人能力层面与元层面的更新机制，并指出当前文献尚未实现经过独立验证的物理递归自我改进。
en_tdlr: This study introduces Physical Recursive Self-Improvement (Physical RSI) and an L0-L5 framework distinguishing capability-level from meta-level updates, revealing that existing literature has not yet demonstrated independently verified physical recursive self-improvement in robots.
